states: All three beds are empty lined trays. Water outlet and wash tray exist. No fresh-water feed hose yet.
All three trays now contain clean light-brown porous granular growing medium. No seeds or plants. The hose route is still empty.

Same medium-filled beds. A slim blue-coupled supply hose now joins the freshwater wall outlet to the EXISTING shared reservoir. Keep the return air gap above the reservoir. Do not add a second pump, tank or bed.

Three medium-filled unplanted zones. The left deep potato bay has a pale translucent liner needing an opaque outer skirt. The rear soybean row is bare medium. The right shallow lettuce shelf has bare medium and an unwicked reservoir edge.

The SAME three beds. A dark opaque foil-backed fabric skirt wraps ONLY the left potato bay sides, with its top still exposed to light. A clean white fabric wick is fitted across the right lettuce tray from its water edge. No plants yet.

The same skirt and wick remain. Small recognizable potato shoots grow in the LEFT bay, young soybean seedlings in the BACK row, little lettuce rosettes in the RIGHT shallow tray. Keep plants confined to their own zones with space between silhouettes.

Leafy potato plants in the left LOW-SIDED bay, with medium just below its low rim; soybean stems at the back are upright but beginning to lean and have NO trellis. The right lettuce tray has green leaves ready to pick. No mature dry bean pods or exposed potato tubers.

A simple additional bolted collar extends the left potato bay sides upward, but its granular medium level is still LOW within the new collar. Same potato foliage. Soybeans still have no trellis. Lettuce unchanged.

The extended potato bay is now filled higher with clean medium around the lower stems; foliage stays above the new rim. Thin straight steel uprights and clean cloth ties support the back soybean row. Lettuce and basin unchanged.
The rear deck is EMPTY, showing its mounting rails. The rover is ready to receive one portable cold case.

One modest rectangular refrigerated sample case sits securely on those rails: simple bolted steel protective shell, reflective insulation, blue refrigerator insert, side handle, an exposed unwrapped heat rejection grille. The case is much smaller than the rover, exactly one case. Everything else unchanged.
Bare shallow wash, no panels, winch or rover. Traversable but soft sloping ground, not a deep cliff or ravine.

Two framed traction panels are laid lengthwise ALONG THE TRAVEL DIRECTION: parallel tracks receding from the foreground toward the background, over the shallow wash, fully supported on ground. Their near ends meet the approach and their far ends reach the firm far bank.

Same correctly oriented tracks. The portable powered winch is attached by a padded sling to the far-bank rock beside the panel ends. A coiled recovery line and hook wait on the far end of the tracks; no line stretched into empty foreground, no rover yet.

The same panels, winch and rock remain. The actual cream/mustard six-wheel rover with its ONE insulated scientific case is now beyond the wash, farther away on the ice-field route. Its wheels face away toward the ice. Winch cable released and stowed. No extra rover in foreground.
Unprepared shallow dusty plot with scattered loose stones. No expansion array or footing.
Loose infill cleared and ground graded. Simple compacted ground and checked flat ceramic footing blocks define the left array area and a smaller empty right equipment pad.

Delivered photovoltaic expansion modules stand on simple straight bolted supports in the LEFT part. The smaller RIGHT equipment pad remains clearly EMPTY for later construction. The original little station array stays far in the background.
Electrolyzer stack positioned and powered/cooled. Its water inlet is capped. No gas manifold or buffer cylinders.
Factory gas-control manifold blocks now fitted on the rack, with two separate gas outlet routes waiting. Water inlet still disconnected. No cylinders.
A service water hose now joins the processor polishing outlet to the electrolyzer water inlet. Same separate gas manifold, no buffer cylinders yet.

Two modest factory buffer cylinders are secured side by side to that rack, each with its own separate keyed gas connection, one hydrogen and one oxygen. No mixing junction. Existing power, cooling and water stay attached.
Complete solar furnace left with its receiver empty of the detachable retort. Workshop press at middle/right. Small equipment footing at far right is empty.

The detachable materials retort is now clamped into the solar receiver, connected by its qualified narrow hydrogen service line to an existing supply connection. Preserve the exact furnace. Press and footing unchanged.

The same retort remains at the furnace. A compact plain straight iron process frame is now bolted onto the separate right footing, ready to receive that retort later. No reactor vessel on this new frame yet.
The small retort is still mounted at the solar furnace; the right process frame is empty.
The furnace receiver cradle at left is now EMPTY. The same small retort has been removed entirely from the scene; the right frame is also empty. Keep both empty seats clearly visible.

The furnace cradle stays empty. The SAME cream retort is now mounted in the RIGHT iron process frame, with its supplied heater/controller and separate metered gas connections. The reactor stays modest and preserves the vessel design; no second retort.
The controlled retort and frame are installed, with gas controls and heater. No separator, radiator or return-water hose yet.
A small imported condenser/separator/dryer core now sits beside the reactor and its gas connections are fitted. Its cooling ports are capped. No panels or water return.

Flat cooling-panel sections on plain bolted supports are installed farther right, joined by qualified coolant tubing to the separator. Large enough area to matter, no huge machine or fans. Water return still capped.
An additional narrow return-water hose now joins the cooled separator outlet to the actual treatment return port at left. The radiator remains.

Exactly the same complete installation commissioned: a small outlet pressure/flow indicator is active, and the purified methane service connector is ready. Preserve all piping and radiator; no new cylinder, plant or tank magically appears.
Two tanks installed, with bare refrigerator mounting brackets and capped feeds. No refrigerator or feed hoses yet.
Two compact refrigerator heads now fitted, one on EACH tank, with existing electrical services. Both feed couplings still capped; both level indicators empty.
Left methane tank connected by its distinct feed line to the purifier at left; left level indicator shows collected liquid. RIGHT tank remains refrigerated but feed-disconnected and empty.
RIGHT oxygen tank connected to the oxygen service outlet at right; right gauge shows collected liquid. LEFT tank remains refrigerated but feed-disconnected and empty.
Both separate feed connections fitted; both tanks show collected liquid. Exactly the same TWO tanks, never a third store or combined gas vessel.
Central alcove empty. Existing freshwater outlet left and paired coolant service ports right.
The simple open steel tank now stands in the central alcove. It is EMPTY and has no internal coil or outer insulation.
A distinct copper-coloured qualified tube coil is fitted INSIDE the tank, ends led to exterior couplings. Tank still empty and uninsulated.
The same empty tank and coil, now wrapped outside in simple foil/felt insulation with a front flap. Its open top still shows no water.
Tank filled with clear non-potable water covering the internal coil, but NO exterior insulation. Same tank and coil.

The water-filled tank has exterior foil/felt insulation and a loose vented cover. Paired coolant leads now visibly connect its coil to the RIGHT wall service ports. No fresh-water hose permanently left in the tank.
Three key-operated selectors all in their normal running positions, small green indicators. Reserve battery module docked and ready.
All three selectors turned to their reserve/isolation positions, small amber indicators. Key removed. The same battery bay and all panel fittings stay unchanged.
Grown crops and reservoir exposed; no thermal screen or reservoir lid yet.

A simple clean fabric thermal screen hangs from the service rail around the outer sides of the growing area, open at the viewing side so plants and reservoir remain visible. The shared reservoir now has a plain fitted steel cover, preserving the aerating return air gap. No exterior reservoir wrap yet.
The same screen and covered shared reservoir. Foil/felt insulation now wraps the reservoir outside, with all supply, drain and pump connections preserved. No second reservoir, no plants moved.

Installed solar panels coated with reddish dust, visibly dull. Their feeder connection is safely UNPLUGGED at the array end; the habitat-side inlet exists. Do not remove the array from its bolted supports.
Same panels now brushed clean with dark reflective photovoltaic faces. The array feed remains unplugged. Same installed processor and dish.
Same cleaned panels, now connected by their actual feeder lead to the habitat inlet. Modest power indicator lit. No duplicate array or portable panel token.
Upright cabin resting partly on temporary steel crib. Ground beside the crib at the permanent support position is unprepared.
A small flat graded patch beside the LOADED crib is prepared for the permanent footing. Crib still carries load. Nothing dug out beneath the loaded feet.

Checked flat ceramic footing blocks and a NEW simple bolted braced support are installed beside the temporary crib, reaching the failed-leg chassis joint. The temporary crib remains in place while fastening completes. Cabin unchanged and upright.

Load now carried by the new permanent braced support and footing. Temporary crib REMOVED. Same roughly vertical cabin, sound legs, tanks, hatch and ladder. No new lander, no rubble, no giant launchpad.
Two lander fill couplings capped. Storage outlets left/right ready; no transfer hoses between outlets and lander yet.
Only LEFT methane transfer hose attached from left store outlet to lander left port; its gauge shows transfer complete. Right port and outlet remain capped.
Only RIGHT oxygen transfer hose attached from right store outlet to right lander port; its gauge shows transfer complete. Left port and outlet remain capped.
Both separate hoses attached to their respective ports, both gauges show transfer complete. Same single spacecraft, no extra tanks.

Harvest maturity: potato foliage yellowing above the dark hilled left bed; back soybean stems supported by the SAME trellis now have dry tan pods and yellowed leaves; right lettuce tray remains living green leaves ready to pick. No exposed potato tubers outside soil. Same structures and plumbing, no new crop bed.
Cold-transfer bench at left ready, flight refrigeration bay at right EMPTY, small membrane locker EMPTY.
One qualified core carrier now locked into refrigerated flight bay, containing TWO separately sealed ice-core liners in their own cradles. Small membrane locker remains empty.
Small original sealed membrane holder secured inside its own locker. Flight core bay remains EMPTY in this independent state.
Both core carrier in its flight refrigeration bay and original membrane holder in its separate locker secured. Exactly two core liners and one membrane holder.
On the ground, prepared console awaiting arming and start; the distant patched round habitat is visible through the window at the correct oblique angle. Mars horizon level.

Ascent underway shown THROUGH the same window: the rounded habitat and ground facilities now small and far below, landscape falling away. Console instruments active. Exactly same cockpit, no floating separate cabin or exterior second rocket.
